description: ENHANCEMENT A: Grow the topic->passage anchor map (deepresearch/fixtures/topic_anchors.json) from one entry to a solid starter set of the most commonly MISUNDERSTOOD teachings/verses about Jesus, each mapped to its correct canonical anchor passage reference(s), with aliases/alternate phrasings mapping to the same anchors. Add bundled kjv/web/asv verse text (deepresearch/fixtures/verses.json) for the anchors you want to be fixture-backed (work fully offline end-to-end); un-fixtured anchors are allowed to degrade to a recorded gap (valid behavior). Document which topics are fixture-backed. This feature owns topic_anchors.json + verses.json + the A tests; FEAT-002 adds the Strong's/commentary data that enriches these same topics.
steps: FIRST, confirm the baseline is green offline so you have a known-good starting point: from /projects/sandbox/Tournament run `unset OPENAI_API_KEY ANTHROPIC_API_KEY && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` and confirm all 54 tests pass. Use /projects/sandbox/Tournament/.venv/bin/python ONLY (NOT the 3.9 python3 on PATH).

Read deepresearch/pipeline.py::resolve_topic_anchors and ::fetch_translations, deepresearch/sources/bible_api.py::_fixture_body, and deepresearch/fixtures/__init__.py to re-confirm the keying rules documented in context.json before editing. Key facts: resolve_topic_anchors matches a topic by re.sub whitespace-collapse + lowercase, so topic_anchors.json keys MUST be lowercase; each value is a LIST of anchor references (parallel-Gospel passages allowed, de-duped downstream). bible_api's offline fixture fallback looks up verses.json by the ORIGINAL single-verse reference string, so verses.json must be keyed exactly as the anchor appears in topic_anchors.json (e.g. 'Matthew 7:1').

Rewrite deepresearch/fixtures/topic_anchors.json to a lowercase-keyed map covering this seed set (verify each reference is correct/canonical; non-denominational, 66-book shared canon). Keep the existing 'turn the other cheek' -> ['Matthew 5:39'] entry. Add at least: 'judge not' -> ['Matthew 7:1']; 'eye of the needle' AND 'camel through the eye of a needle' -> ['Matthew 19:24','Mark 10:25','Luke 18:25']; 'money is the root of all evil' AND 'love of money' -> ['1 Timothy 6:10']; 'faith without works' -> ['James 2:17','James 2:26']; 'i never knew you' -> ['Matthew 7:23']; 'render unto caesar' -> ['Matthew 22:21','Mark 12:17']; 'the unforgivable sin' AND 'blasphemy against the holy spirit' -> ['Matthew 12:31','Mark 3:29']; 'ask and it will be given' -> ['Matthew 7:7']; 'narrow gate' AND 'narrow road' -> ['Matthew 7:13-14']; 'let the dead bury their dead' -> ['Matthew 8:22','Luke 9:60']; 'i came not to bring peace but a sword' -> ['Matthew 10:34']; 'the first will be last' -> ['Matthew 20:16','Matthew 19:30']; 'whoever is not against us is for us' -> ['Mark 9:40']; 'take up your cross' -> ['Matthew 16:24']; 'born again' -> ['John 3:3']; 'the truth will set you free' -> ['John 8:32']; 'i am the way the truth and the life' -> ['John 14:6']; 'do not worry about tomorrow' -> ['Matthew 6:34']; 'where two or three are gathered' -> ['Matthew 18:20']. Use good judgment to adjust references for canonical correctness and add a few more natural alias keys that normalize to the same anchors. Multiple aliases pointing to the same anchor list is fine.

Decide the fixture-backed subset (anchors with bundled verse text so they produce scripture offline). Pick a solid subset you will add verse text + tests for - AT LEAST these fixture-backed topics covering distinct anchors so end-to-end tests have real scripture: 'judge not' (Matthew 7:1), 'ask and it will be given' (Matthew 7:7), 'narrow gate' (Matthew 7:13-14), 'born again' (John 3:3), 'i am the way the truth and the life' (John 14:6), plus keep 'turn the other cheek' (Matthew 5:39) fixture-backed. You may fixture-back more; any anchor you leave un-fixtured will degrade to a recorded gap offline (valid). Coordinate so FEAT-002 adds matching Strong's/commentary where it enriches these.

For EVERY anchor reference in your fixture-backed subset, add an entry to deepresearch/fixtures/verses.json keyed by the exact reference string, with kjv, web, and asv objects each containing reference, text (the correct PUBLIC-DOMAIN verse text for that translation), translation, and url (match the existing bible-api.com URL shape, e.g. https://bible-api.com/John%203:3?translation=kjv). Use ONLY public-domain KJV/WEB/ASV wording. For a range anchor like Matthew 7:13-14, key verses.json by 'Matthew 7:13-14' and include the combined passage text. Keep the file valid JSON and preserve existing Matthew 5:17 / Matthew 5:39 entries unchanged.

Add new tests in tests/test_end_to_end.py (follow the existing _run/_assert_valid_and_populated pattern, dry-run, offline, load_env_file=False): (a) end-to-end dry-run for at least TWO new fixture-backed topics (e.g. 'judge not' and 'born again') asserting query_kind=='topic', resolved_reference is None, translations non-empty with the expected anchor reference, resolved_references equals the expected anchor list, and _assert_valid_and_populated passes (schema-valid). (b) An alias-normalization test asserting resolve_topic_anchors returns the same anchor list for an alias and for differently-cased/whitespaced phrasings (e.g. 'Judge Not', '  judge   not ', and 'camel through the eye of a needle' vs 'eye of the needle'). (c) An unmapped-topic graceful-degradation test: run dry-run on a topic that is NOT in the map (e.g. 'the meaning of grace') and assert it still produces a schema-valid dossier (translations may be empty, a gap is recorded, no crash).

Run the offline suite again and confirm green: `unset OPENAI_API_KEY ANTHROPIC_API_KEY && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q`. Do NOT weaken any existing assertion (the existing test_end_to_end 'turn the other cheek' test asserting resolved_references==['Matthew 5:39'] MUST still pass - keep that anchor single-valued).

Add a short note to README.md (Architecture stage 2 area or a new subsection) listing how many topics the map now covers and which are fixture-backed (work fully offline) vs which degrade to a gap offline.
acceptance_criteria: deepresearch/fixtures/topic_anchors.json is valid JSON, lowercase-keyed, covers the seed set with alias keys, and preserves 'turn the other cheek' -> ['Matthew 5:39'].

deepresearch/fixtures/verses.json contains valid kjv/web/asv public-domain text for every fixture-backed anchor, keyed by the exact anchor reference string, and preserves the existing Matthew 5:17/5:39 entries.
Running `unset OPENAI_API_KEY ANTHROPIC_API_KEY && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` passes with no network, including the new A tests and all pre-existing tests unchanged.

A dry-run on at least two new fixture-backed topics yields a schema-valid dossier carrying scripture at the expected anchor(s); an unmapped topic still yields a schema-valid dossier with a recorded gap and no crash.
README documents topic-map coverage and the fixture-backed vs gap-degrading distinction.
findings: Grew topic_anchors.json from 1 entry to 35 lowercase keys covering the seed set plus natural aliases (multiple aliases map to the same anchor list; parallel-Gospel passages included where canonical). Preserved 'turn the other cheek' -> ['Matthew 5:39'] single-valued. Fixture-backed subset in verses.json: Matthew 5:17 (kept), Matthew 5:39 (kept), Matthew 7:1, Matthew 7:7, Matthew 7:13-14 (range, combined passage text), John 3:3, John 14:6 - each with public-domain KJV/WEB/ASV text keyed by the exact single-verse/range reference string (matches bible_api._fixture_body lookup, which uses the ORIGINAL reference, not the context-expanded passage). Added 4 tests to tests/test_end_to_end.py: judge-not and born-again fixture-backed end-to-end dry-runs (schema-valid, correct resolved_references, 3 translations each), an alias/normalization test (case + whitespace + distinct alias phrasings resolve to same anchor list; unmapped yields []), and an unmapped-topic graceful-degradation test (schema-valid dossier, empty translations, gaps recorded, no crash). NOTE for FEAT-002/003: an unmapped topic produces NO bible_api gap because fetch_translations returns early on empty references; it records strongs/commentary/integrity gaps instead, so the degradation test asserts gaps are non-empty rather than requiring a bible_api-specific gap. Updated README stage-2 section with topic-map coverage (35 keys) and the fixture-backed vs gap-degrading distinction. Full offline suite: 58 passed (was 54), zero network, using .venv 3.12 interpreter.
